invariantSafetyChannels.meaning: Family-relevant gravity, curvature, shear and environmental state must remain observable or bounded.
Navigation and endpoint/state uncertainty must remain explicit rather than being hidden by interface abstraction.
The interface must expose enough future state to complete detection, validation, command, actuation and safe exit before irreversible hazard entry.
Recovery/abort authority must remain physically and procedurally reserved from nominal performance optimization.
Required hazards must have a direct or independently validated guard channel; sensor silence is not positive safety evidence.

abortEmbodiment: guarded manual and automatic abort initiation
generatorRules: Do not reduce the interface to a single speed number.
Show uncertainty and recovery reserve as first-class controls.
Use familiar industrial form only when the manufacturer basis actually resolves to this family.

navigationRepresentation: hazard state expressed through turbulence/interference analogues where culturally appropriate
serviceEnvironment: continuous immersion or pressure-balanced wet bay
generatorRules: Represent route safety through native wet machinery rather than dry terrestrial consoles.
Do not treat pressure or chemistry alarms as cosmetic; they can directly collapse control authority.

navigationRepresentation: route certificate tied to cooldown state
abortEmbodiment: thermal isolation and rapid state dump
generatorRules: Transit readiness must include thermal state and contraction alignment.
Do not depict warm human-access service as routine without a conversion bay.
Do not translate the architecture into rigid dry cabinets.
Show pressure and buoyancy state as part of navigation/control readiness.

sensorArchitecture: independent guard tissue or physically isolated fallback sensors
abortEmbodiment: sacrificial shedding or hard biological isolation where appropriate
generatorRules: Biological machinery remains machinery with measurable tolerances and failure states.
Healing never implies automatic recertification.
Preserve physical independence for the last abort/guard channel.

abortEmbodiment: rapid preload release or mode collapse
generatorRules: Do not represent resonance state as ordinary electrical voltage alone.
Navigation/control failures should emerge from alignment, mode purity and reference drift as well as power loss.
Advanced adaptive machinery does not erase engineering constraints.
Never equate self-configuration with self-certification.
Retain a mechanically or physically independent last-resort recovery path when the named source allows one.

scalingModel.principle: Control and maintenance complexity scales with protected volume, distribution span, coordination delay, independent sensor ancestry, actuator count, recovery segmentation and service-environment burden rather than with vessel mass alone.

canonGuards: Specific named race, vessel, manufacturer, installation and technology sources outrank generic technology-basis embodiment.
Technology-basis embodiment changes physical implementation, not the invariant safety information required by the selected transit family.
No technology basis may erase gravity/environment state, uncertainty, actionable lookahead, protected recovery or hazard observability.
No unresolved named profile may acquire a transit-family assignment from vocabulary similarity, technology basis or generator convenience.
A human-readable translation layer must not overwrite the alien/native control state or its provenance.
Biological healing, adaptive self-reconfiguration and automated repair do not imply recertification.
Redundant displays sharing one upstream sensor/fusion root do not count as independent hazard observation.
Maintenance doctrine must preserve the service environment and contamination/reference constraints of the resolved basis.
More advanced Path level increases metrology, automation and margins but does not convert a species/manufacturer basis into terrestrial machinery.
PROPOSED scaling mathematics and generic embodiments are generator aids, not retroactive historical canon.
